reviewScope: DR-112 signed-index-trust-contract v7 only. This is not a DR-111 or compatibility-matrices review. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, qualify or demonstrate anything, authorize docs/v2/implementation/, or apply or seal the candidate.
summary: The claimed v6 repairs are present at the named surfaces: outcomeBranchDiscipline precedes fallback, the live RECOVER-COMMIT branch is whenActiveFailure and ACTIVE-qualified, PRESENT/INSTALL/COMMIT have structured normativeExclusion fields, the roster uses whole paths, and the finalized Codex v5 verdict is digest-pinned. Acceptance is still withheld because the new branch algorithm does not preserve the authenticated payload-kind routing predicate. For an INACTIVE recovery-typed PRESENT, an ordinary TRUSTED-entry member's whenInactive branch is true solely from envelope standing, while the recovery staging member's branchless guard is also true. Four source states therefore have refused ENVELOPE-INACTIVE and accepted staging outcomes for the same input; from TRUSTED, the same bypass emits ENVELOPE-INACTIVE rather than the declared unmatched-recovery fallback. Neither reading enters TRUSTED, installs bytes, or publishes a root, so this is not a blocker, but the state machine and fixture oracle are not deterministic. At 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, this candidate is REJECTED; DR-112 remains OPEN and no implementation is authorized.

shouldFix.title: Branch selection bypasses the authenticated payload-kind discriminator
shouldFix.measurement: outcomeBranchDiscipline says whenInactive is true iff that member's TRUSTED-entry/envelope standing is INACTIVE; unlike whenActiveSuccess, it does not require the member guard or any routing predicate. Transitions 0-2 require authenticated payloadKind=ordinary in their guards, but their whenInactive branches do not. Transition 6 requires payloadKind=recovery and is branchless. Therefore, with envelope standing INACTIVE and a valid recovery-typed payload: ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED, ST-EXPIRED, ST-STALE-REVOCATION, and ST-QUORUM-LOST each match an ordinary member's refused ENVELOPE-INACTIVE branch and transition 6's accepted staging guard simultaneously. defaultTransition says each true member fires but supplies no cross-member winner. From ST-TRUSTED, transition 1's whenInactive fires even though recovery kind makes its ordinary guard inapplicable, so the event reports ENVELOPE-INACTIVE instead of the PRESENT fallback's PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE for a recovery payload with no staging member.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: The contract's authenticated discriminator, FC-RECOVER, FC-PAYLOAD-KIND-DISJOINT, and the historical repair statement all require ordinary and recovery PRESENT paths to remain disjoint. The new algorithm makes them overlap exactly while the envelope dependency is INACTIVE, producing incompatible audit outcomes and either staging or refusing the same recovery input. Neither outcome admits install bytes, enters ST-TRUSTED, publishes a root, fetches, refreshes, or mutates the lock; the accepted alternative only stages a recovery payload while preserving state. The defect is therefore not a fail-open blocker, but an implementation or fixture cannot conform without inventing member-routing precedence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define a member-applicability phase before outcome-branch evaluation, preserving authenticated discriminators such as payloadKind, or make each PRESENT whenInactive predicate explicitly require payloadKind=ordinary. Then define cross-member selection so exactly one member can fire. Pin traces showing: INACTIVE+ordinary on a TRUSTED-entry member yields ENVELOPE-INACTIVE; INACTIVE+recovery in UNBOOTSTRAPPED/EXPIRED/STALE/QUORUM yields only accepted staging; and recovery from TRUSTED, where no staging member exists, reaches PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE rather than the ordinary member's inactive branch.

attackResults.claimedCodexV6S1Repair: PARTIAL FAIL at SITCV7-S1. The requested branch-before-fallback algorithm, ACTIVE-qualified whenActiveFailure, and three normative exclusions exist and remove the old fallback-reason ambiguity. The algorithm nevertheless evaluates whenInactive without first establishing member applicability, breaking authenticated ordinary-versus-recovery dispatch.
attackResults.inactiveNamedMemberFallback: PASS narrowly. A genuinely applicable named whenInactive branch precedes fallback and cannot emit PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE, INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED, or RECOVERY-COMMIT-REFUSED. SITCV7-S1 is a distinct pre-branch routing defect: an inapplicable ordinary member can become active solely because the envelope is INACTIVE.
attackResults.defaultTransitionOrdering: PASS. defaultTransition explicitly applies outcomeBranchDiscipline first and reaches fallback only after no true structured branch or branchless guard remains.
attackResults.recoverCommitBranch: PASS. Transition 16 has whenInactive, whenActiveSuccess, and whenActiveFailure; no live whenFailed key remains. whenActiveFailure requires ACTIVE and failure of another recoveryTrustedEntry conjunct.

The frozen Codex v6 verdict is COMPLETE REJECT with 0 blockers, SITCV6-S1, and SITCV6-A1/A2. v7 records the exact paths, digests, verdicts, and qualified ledgers, and the two roster advisories are correctly identified as the same issue.

attackResults.machineCoverage: PASS for relation coverage, FAIL for determinism at SITCV7-S1. There are 7 states, 9 events, 19 transition members, 43 named pairs, 20 fallback-only pairs, five multi-member pairs, and all nine event fallbacks. The four PRESENT overlaps cease to be disjoint under the new INACTIVE branch rule.
attackResults.recoveryPayloadDispatch: FAIL at SITCV7-S1. A recovery-typed payload from four staging states is simultaneously an accepted staging member and an ordinary member's inactive refusal. The recovery input never reaches ST-TRUSTED, but its event outcome and staging side effect are not single-valued.
attackResults.recoveryTrustedEntry: PASS. RECOVER-COMMIT continues to require ACTIVE standing, the full seven-conjunct recovery authority shape, role/key, normal threshold, time, freshness, anti-rollback, DR-103 byte checks, and DR-112 envelope verification.
attackResults.refusalVocabulary: PASS for closure. The 13 declared values are unique and all have structured producers; no structured refused outcome omits a reason and no structured accepted outcome carries one. Exact PRESENT routing fails separately at SITCV7-S1.
attackResults.offlineContinuation: PASS. Independent evaluation of all 343 CORE/INDEX/COMPONENT state triples yields 340 refusals, 3 permitted already-running outcomes, and 0 defaults; every permissive outcome requires CORE and COMPONENT TRUSTED.
attackResults.sourceAndCarryIntegrity: PASS. The non-COORD governing pins, live COORD/file-08 remeasurements, historical inherited COORD pin, both verbatim carries, and the unique DR-112 row reproduce.
attackResults.implicitNetworkOrLockMutation: PASS. Missing, invalid, inactive, recovery-failed, and nontrusted paths contain no implicit fetch/refresh or lock mutation authorization.
attackResults.roleDeferralAndNumbers: PASS. Five separate trust roles remain; repair-media rides DR-110, replay rides DR-113, and quorum, clock/freshness, emergency, and waiver values remain reserved.
